questions.prompt: The primary circadian time setter he emphasizes is:
choices: A Only caffeine timing.
B Light intensity via the eyes acting on the SCN (suprachiasmatic nucleus).
C Television volume.
D Shoe size.
questions.explain: Bright light to the eyes triggers the SCN and sets the ~24-hour cycle.

questions.prompt: Besides light, an important peripheral clock is:
choices: A Only fingernail growth.
B The digestive system / meal timing as a peripheral time cue.
C Unused in humans.
D Only lunar phases.
questions.explain: Peripheral clocks—especially digestive—also set time cues.

questions.prompt: On intermittent fasting versus calorie control for weight:
choices: A IF is always magically superior to calorie control.
B It does not seem superior to regular calorie control for weight/body composition.
C IF forbids all protein forever.
D Late-night eating always raises metabolic rate.
questions.explain: IF is not shown superior to ordinary calorie control for weight.

choices: A Protein timing never matters for anyone.
B You must ingest protein immediately post-workout or gains are lost—an overstated urgency.
C Only carbs post-workout matter.
D Fasting after lifting is mandatory.
questions.explain: He critiques the idea that missing immediate post-workout protein nullifies the session.

B Overall diet quality first—do not major in the minors.
C Only pre-bed protein for everyone.
